title: Scorecard weights
decision: Score = usage growth {w_usage} + new developers {w_newdev} + SA engagement {w_eng} + commit burn {w_burn}, each measured as a percentile against all accounts.
why: Usage growth is the clearest sign a customer is already moving work onto the platform, so it counts most.
possibly: Possibly we can replace hand-set weights with a model trained on which accounts actually grew.

title: 90-day window
decision: Usage growth and SA meetings look back {win_usage} days; new developers look back {win_newdev} days.
why: A quarter smooths out weekly noise but still reflects today. New teams show up fast, so a month catches them early.
possibly: Possibly we can test 30, 60 and 90-day windows and keep the one that best predicts growth.

title: Pool of funds formula
decision: Pool of funds = unused commit + open pipeline. Expected value = score ÷ 100 × pool of funds.
why: Unused commit protects the renewal and open deals are new revenue; together they are the money our help could unlock.
possibly: Possibly we can add forecast usage growth, not just today's gaps.

title: Capacity
decision: The team can actively cover the top {capacity} accounts by expected value.
why: Headcount is fixed, so dedicated help goes where expected value is highest; everyone else gets a scaled motion.
possibly: Possibly we can set capacity from real SA/FDE hours per engagement instead of a flat count.

title: Flag thresholds
decision: Commit at Risk under {car_pace} of pace (after 25% of the term); Renewal Window ≤ {renewal_days} days; Usage Spike ≥ {spike}×; New Developers ≥ {newdev_min} in {win_newdev} days.
why: Each flag is a "why now" signal tied to an action: recover burn, prepare the renewal, support a launch, or onboard a new team.
possibly: Possibly we can tune each threshold so it fires only as often as the team can act on it each week.

title: Quadrant cut-offs
decision: High score = {score_high}+; high value = pool of funds of {pool_high}+. Together they pick one of four motions.
why: Splitting likelihood from size stops big-but-unlikely and small-but-likely accounts from getting the same help.
possibly: Possibly we can revisit the cut-offs each quarter as capacity and the customer base change.

title: Holdout
decision: {holdout_share} of Commit Burn Sprint accounts are picked at random, measured, but not enrolled.
why: Comparing helped vs. similar unhelped customers shows the program's real lift, not growth that would have happened anyway.
possibly: Possibly we can rotate the holdout each cycle so no customer goes without help for long.
